Alan Turing was a British mathematician, computer scientist, logician, cryptanalyst, philosopher, and theoretical biologist. "The Turing machine was invented in 1936 by Alan Turing, who called it an 'a-machine' (automatic machine)." Does a machine exist that can determine whether any arbitrary machine on its tape ever prints a given symbol?"

During World War II, Turing made crucial contributions to codebreaking efforts. "Turing played a crucial role in cracking intercepted coded messages that enabled the Allies to defeat the Axis powers in many crucial engagements, including the Battle of the Atlantic." His work at Bletchley Park was particularly significant: "He devised a number of techniques for speeding the breaking of German ciphers, including improvements to the pre-war Polish bomba method, an electromechanical machine that could find settings for the Enigma machine."

Turing's work on early computers was foundational. "After the war, Turing worked at the National Physical Laboratory, where he designed the Automatic Computing Engine (ACE), one of the first designs for a stored-program computer." His theoretical contributions extended to artificial intelligence: "Turing proposed the Turing test as a criterion of intelligence, a concept that has had a lasting influence on the philosophy of artificial intelligence."

The impact of Turing's work is profound and far-reaching. "Turing is widely considered to be the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence."
